rationale: All four lenses plus the standards audit ran with parseable output over a non-oversized diff; 17 blocking findings survive, including four critical ones: `--agent`/`--scope`/`--mode` now divert the shipped interactive invocation into the headless branch and hard-fail, the interactive skills wizard still drops unavailable ids silently, skill readability is only proven inside the write loop, and the headless assistants catalog omits marketplace assistants so a valid identifier is reported as unavailable. Two candidates stayed reachability-unconfirmed and are capped at major — the headless skills catalog's unfiltered `listPaginated` (server-side default contents not observable from the repo) and the re-auth prompt reachable from flag-triggered headless mode at a TTY — which is why confidence is medium rather than high; standards reported no coverage gap. 4 findings deferred as pre-existing (unregister ignores stored agentTargets; removal failures swallowed; the notice names a non-existent `codemie assistants setup` command, duplicated from showDisclaimer; unlocked load-modify-save config writes) — recorded in docs/superpowers/tasks/2026-09-18-codemie-assistant-skill-registration/code-review-deferred.md; 19 findings dismissed as noise, unreachable or spec-sanctioned.

business_review.item: Approach: non-interactive branch added to setupAssistants and setupSkills via headless flags on existing commands; no new verb
business_review.notes: Branches at assistants/setup/index.ts:74-76 and skills/setup/index.ts:108-110; flags added on the existing factories; no new command file.

business_review.item: Approach: headless when any headless flag or -y is present, or when process.stdin.isTTY is not true
business_review.notes: isHeadlessMode (shared/headless.ts:22-28) short-circuits on non-TTY then ORs the flags; both call sites pass process.stdin.isTTY === true.

business_review.item: Approach: headless inputs explicit, never inferred — --scope, --agent and (assistants) --mode required; auto-detection never runs
business_review.notes: requireFlag/parseScopeFlag/parseRegistrationModeFlag validate up front; headless uses parseAgentSetupTarget, not resolveAgentSetupTargets.

business_review.item: Approach: multi-value flags are comma-separated, matching the existing --agent <agents>
business_review.notes: parseListFlag splits, trims and de-dupes on comma (shared/headless.ts:63-71).

business_review.item: Approach: identifiers resolve by id, slug, or exact name, case-insensitively; a name matching several is an ambiguity error, never a pick
business_review.notes: resolveIdentifiers covers all three, but duplicate ids/slugs silently last-wins (CR-012) and the skills catalog carries no slug, so slug resolution is unreachable for skills.

business_review.item: Approach: fail-fast is one contract for both modes — pre-flight resolves every identifier and confirms every target before the first filesystem write
business_review.notes: Assistants side fixed (fetchAssistantsByIds propagates, RegistrationItemNotFoundError, executeWithSpinnerStrict), but the skills wizard still drops unavailable ids (CR-015) and skills pre-flight is inside the write loop (CR-016).

business_review.item: Approach: atomicity stops at pre-flight — a failure after writing begins aborts and reports which items were already written, with no rollback
business_review.notes: registerAllOrAbort writes sequentially and throws PartialRegistrationError carrying the written names; no rollback code added, per spec.

business_review.item: Approach: the skills notice is informational — headless prints the same text and continues; the interactive Enter gate is unchanged
business_review.notes: printSkillsNotice uses console.log with no stdin read; showDisclaimer untouched.

business_review.item: Approach: both wiring sites gain the flags together (cli/commands/setup.ts and agents/core/AgentCLI.ts)
business_review.notes: Both sites call the same factories (setup.ts:27-28, AgentCLI.ts:115-116), so flags declared inside them reach both surfaces.

business_review.item: AC: a single non-interactive command registers several assistants and/or skills with no prompt and no raw-mode call
business_review.notes: Happy path is prompt-free, but getAuthenticatedClient can still reach promptReauthentication whose only guard is !process.stdin.isTTY (CR-017).

business_review.item: AC: a requested item not available to the authenticated user aborts the entire run with a named, actionable error and a non-zero exit, in both modes
business_review.notes: Holds headlessly and in the assistants wizard; the skills wizard still filters unknown ids out silently (CR-015). Marketplace assistants also produce a false unavailability error (CR-002).

business_review.item: AC: the abort happens before any artifact is written under .claude/.codex/.gemini and before config is saved
business_review.notes: Identifier resolution and auth precede the writes, but fetchSkillById runs inside the registerAllOrAbort callback, so a per-skill failure aborts after earlier items were written (CR-016).

business_review.item: AC: authentication is verified before any side effect
business_review.notes: getAuthenticatedClient runs before the catalog fetch and every write in both headless branches; flag validation rejects earlier still. Only console output precedes it.

business_review.item: AC: missing --scope, --agent, or assistant registration mode in headless mode each fail with an error naming the missing flag
business_review.notes: requireFlag throws ConfigurationError('Missing required flag: <flag>'); invalid --mode/--scope are also named. Asserted per flag in both headless test files.

business_review.item: AC: an identifier matching no item, and a name matching several, produce distinct typed errors
business_review.notes: RegistrationItemNotFoundError vs AmbiguousIdentifierError, both new CodeMieError subclasses; covered by shared/__tests__/identifier-resolution.test.ts.

business_review.item: AC: a mid-write failure aborts and reports the already-written items by name
business_review.notes: PartialRegistrationError lists written names plus the cause message, surfaced by handleSetupError; covered by registration-writes.test.ts. Config-record consequence tracked as CR-011.

business_review.item: AC: with no headless flags at a TTY, wizard behaviour — search, panels, re-registration — is unchanged
business_review.notes: isHeadlessMode treats the pre-existing --agent (and --scope/--mode) as headless triggers, so `setup assistants --agent claude` at a TTY now errors instead of running the wizard (CR-009).

business_review.item: AC: both `codemie setup ...` and `codemie-<agent> setup ...` expose the same flags
business_review.notes: Flags are identical because both wiring sites share the factories, but the per-agent surface cannot use them without repeating --agent since hostAgent is ignored headlessly (CR-005).

findings.title: Headless assistant catalog paged five at a time
findings.problem: fetchAllVisibleAssistants pages the entire visible assistant catalog with per_page: CONFIG.ITEMS_PER_PAGE, and CONFIG.ITEMS_PER_PAGE is 5 (src/cli/commands/shared/selection/constants.ts:60), while also requesting minimal_response: false so every page carries full assistant payloads. The skills counterpart uses ALL_VISIBLE_PER_PAGE = 100 for the same operation (src/cli/commands/skills/setup/data.ts:50).
findings.impact: Every headless invocation performs ceil(N/5) sequential API round-trips with full payloads just to resolve one or two identifiers: an org with 500 visible assistants costs 100 serial requests per `codemie setup assistants --assistant X ...` run, making scripted/CI registration slow and rate-limit prone.
findings.recommendation: Use a bulk page size (100, matching the skills fetcher) and minimal_response: true for the resolution-only crawl, since resolveIdentifiers needs only id, slug and name.

findings.title: Headless catalog omits marketplace assistants
findings.problem: fetchAllVisibleAssistants pages only scope: API_SCOPE.VISIBLE_TO_USER. The interactive wizard fetches two scopes — API_SCOPE.VISIBLE_TO_USER for the project panel and API_SCOPE.MARKETPLACE for the marketplace panel (src/cli/commands/assistants/setup/data.ts:84-85) — so any assistant a user can install from the marketplace panel is absent from the headless catalog handed to resolveIdentifiers.
findings.impact: A valid, installable marketplace assistant named with --assistant fails with RegistrationItemNotFoundError, `No assistant found matching "X"`. This inverts the task's headline requirement: instead of stopping when an assistant is genuinely unavailable, the command reports an available one as unavailable, and that class of assistant cannot be registered headlessly at all.
findings.recommendation: Page API_SCOPE.MARKETPLACE as well and merge both result sets (de-duplicating by id) before calling resolveIdentifiers, so the headless catalog is the union the wizard shows.

findings.title: Project scope flags silently ignored headlessly
findings.problem: --project and --all-projects are declared on the command (src/cli/commands/assistants/setup/index.ts:50-51) and `options` is passed into createDataFetcher from the headless branch (index.ts:200), but fetchAllVisibleAssistants hardcodes scope: API_SCOPE.VISIBLE_TO_USER and filters: { search: '' } with no project filter, so neither flag has any effect on the headless path.
findings.impact: Name resolution spans projects the user explicitly excluded: a name identifier can resolve to an assistant from an excluded project, or raise AmbiguousIdentifierError for a name the project filter would have made unique. The flag is accepted without warning, so a script cannot tell its filter was dropped.
findings.recommendation: Either thread options.project/options.allProjects into the fetchAllVisibleAssistants filters, or reject the combination up front with a ConfigurationError stating that --project/--all-projects are unsupported alongside --assistant.

findings.title: Headless entry points exceed 50-line limit
findings.problem: code-quality.md 'Code Structure Guidelines' requires functions under 50 lines. setupAssistantsHeadless spans 59 lines (src/cli/commands/assistants/setup/index.ts:185-243) and setupSkillsHeadless spans 62 lines (src/cli/commands/skills/setup/index.ts:210-271). Each mixes flag parsing and validation, config and client loading, catalog fetch, identifier resolution, the additive-scoping computation, the apply call, the config save and result printing in one body.
findings.impact: Blocks the documented project standard, and keeps two independently testable units — the flag-validation prologue and the additive-scoping reconciliation — reachable only through the whole command path, which is exactly why CR-006 and CR-013 have no direct coverage.
findings.recommendation: Extract the flag parse/validate prologue (parseListFlag/requireFlag/parseScopeFlag/mode) and the additive-scoping split into named helpers alongside shared/headless.ts and shared/identifier-resolution.ts, leaving each entry point as the orchestration sequence.

findings.title: hostAgent accepted but never used headlessly
findings.problem: Both headless entry points take hostAgent and use it only in a logger.debug call (assistants/setup/index.ts:188, skills/setup/index.ts:213), then call requireFlag(options.agent, '--agent') unconditionally (assistants:193, skills:216). The interactive path resolves this with no flag at all: resolveAgentSetupTargets returns [hostAgent] when value is undefined (src/cli/commands/shared/agent-targets.ts:34-37), and AgentCLI wires the adapter name in as hostAgent (src/agents/core/AgentCLI.ts:115-116).
findings.impact: `codemie-claude setup assistants --assistant X --scope global --mode agent -y` fails with `Missing required flag: --agent` even though the invocation unambiguously determines the target, so the per-agent shortcut surface cannot use headless mode without redundantly repeating information the command already holds.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the target as parseAgentSetupTarget(options.agent ?? hostAgent) and only requireFlag when both are absent, keeping the explicit-inputs contract for the generic `codemie setup` surface.

findings.title: Cross-scope registrations copied into target scope
findings.problem: The headless assistants branch loads the registered set with loadRegisteredAssistants() (index.ts:197), which merges StorageScope.GLOBAL and StorageScope.LOCAL and de-dupes by id (src/utils/config.ts:1488-1504). untouchedRegistered (index.ts:217) is therefore the cross-scope complement of the request, and it is written back into the single scope named by --scope via saveAssistantsToProjectConfig (index.ts:240), which overwrites that scope's codemieAssistants wholesale (src/utils/config.ts:919-927). The skills branch does this correctly with ConfigLoader.loadSkillsByScope(storageScope, ...) (skills/setup/index.ts:223).
findings.impact: `--scope local` rewrites the project config with every globally-registered assistant copied in, and `--scope global` copies local-only ones into ~/.codemie, so the two registries drift and entries claim registration in a scope whose artifact files never existed. The interactive path only carried forward the ids the user actually selected, so this is an amplification introduced by the headless branch, and project configs are commonly committed to VCS.
findings.recommendation: Load the registered set with ConfigLoader.loadAssistantsByScope(storageScope, workingDir) so untouchedRegistered contains only entries that already belong to the scope being written, matching the skills branch.

findings.title: --mode skill never exercised by any test
findings.problem: applyChanges resolves the mode as registrationModes.get(fullAssistant.id) || REGISTRATION_MODE.AGENT (index.ts:288), and every case in the new assistants headless test uses mode: 'agent' — identical to that fallback. No test passes mode: 'skill', and no assertion inspects the mode argument handed to registerAssistant or the registrationMode of the saved entries (the mode-specific tests only cover a missing and a 'bogus' value).
findings.impact: Dropping or ignoring --mode is invisible to the suite. `--assistant X --mode skill` could register X as a Claude subagent and persist registrationMode: 'agent'; ConfigLoader.loadAssistantsByScope picks .claude/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md vs .claude/agents/<slug>.md from that field (src/utils/config.ts:970-973), so a wrong value silently prunes the entry on the next load.
findings.recommendation: Add a headless case with mode: 'skill' asserting registerAssistant is called with 'skill' and that the persisted entry carries registrationMode: 'skill'.

findings.title: No test covers command-level partial failure
findings.problem: registration-writes.test.ts only calls registerAllOrAbort directly and asserts the returned array plus PartialRegistrationError.written/.cause; it never touches the config save. The new headless tests never make registerSkill/registerAssistant reject, and no test in the repo invokes the setup command action (grep for parseAsync/.parse( under src/cli finds only profile/__tests__/index.test.ts:132).
findings.impact: The orphaned-artifact regression behind CR-011 has no failing test: nothing asserts what happens to the first of three items when the second fails, in either direction (config recorded, or file removed). Previously the loop skipped failures and still saved the successes, so the behaviour change is entirely unpinned.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that drives applyChanges/applySkillChanges with the second of three writes rejecting and asserts the intended outcome for the first item — either that the save is called with it, or that its generated file was removed.

findings.title: Existing --agent invocation now hard-fails
findings.problem: isHeadlessMode returns true when any of flags.yes, flags.scope, flags.agent, flags.assistant, flags.skill or flags.mode is set, and both call sites pass the whole options object (assistants/setup/index.ts:74, skills/setup/index.ts:108). --agent <agents> is a pre-existing, documented option on both commands (assistants/setup/index.ts:52), so `codemie setup assistants --agent claude` at a TTY now diverts into the headless branch and aborts at requireFlag(options.assistant, '--assistant'). The function's own doc-comment also says 'stdout is not a TTY' while both call sites feed process.stdin.isTTY.
findings.impact: A previously working invocation of a shipped CLI surface fails with `Missing required flag: --assistant` (and `--skill` for the skills command), with no compatibility shim or deprecation path; users and scripts that pass --agent to preselect the target while still choosing items interactively lose the selection UI entirely. As a direct consequence resolveAgentSetupTargets(options.agent, hostAgent) at assistants/setup/index.ts:151 can no longer receive a defined options.agent.
findings.recommendation: Trigger headless mode only on the flags that are new and unambiguous (--assistant/--skill, plus -y), leaving --agent/--scope/--mode as wizard preselectors; keep the non-TTY short-circuit. Fix the stdout/stdin doc-comment, and correct MESSAGES.SETUP.OPTION_YES ('Run non-interactively, skipping all prompts') which promises defaults -y alone does not supply.

findings.title: New exported helper has no JSDoc
findings.problem: code-quality.md 'Comments & Documentation' requires JSDoc on all public APIs and lists 'Omit docs from public API' as a Don't. The newly exported executeWithSpinnerStrict<T> has none, even though its sibling registerAllOrAbort in the same hunk (helpers.ts:72) does, and its only behavioural difference from the adjacent executeWithSpinner is that it rethrows instead of returning null.
findings.impact: Blocks the documented coding standard, and this is precisely the case the rule exists for: two near-identical exports whose contracts differ only in failure behaviour, where picking the wrong one silently changes whether a failed registration is reported as success.
findings.recommendation: Add a JSDoc block on executeWithSpinnerStrict stating that it rethrows after invoking onError, in contrast to executeWithSpinner which swallows and returns null.

findings.title: Partial registration leaves unrecorded artifacts
findings.problem: registerAllOrAbort throws PartialRegistrationError out of applyChanges/applySkillChanges, which is above the config save in both callers (assistants/setup/index.ts:240, skills/setup/index.ts:259), so nothing the batch already wrote is ever recorded. applySkillChanges is worse on the re-register path: it unregisters every toReregister skill first (skills/setup/index.ts:301-303) and only then builds and writes allToRegister, so a failure partway through re-registration has already deleted a working skill's files.
findings.impact: Files written for items 1..N-1 stay on disk with no config entry, so the CLI cannot list or unregister them (registerAllOrAbort's own doc-comment states items already written stay written). On the re-register path an existing, working registration is deleted and never rewritten while the config still claims it, so loadSkillsByScope prunes it on the next read and the skill silently disappears. The previous loop skipped failures and still saved the successes.
findings.recommendation: Persist the successfully written items before rethrowing — save [...untouchedRegistered, ...results] from within the catch — so the config always reflects what is on disk, and defer the unregister of toReregister items until their replacement has been fetched and written.

findings.title: Duplicate ids and slugs silently last-wins
findings.problem: resolveIdentifiers builds byId and bySlug with plain Map.set (lines 34 and 37), so a second catalog entry sharing an id or slug overwrites the first; only name collisions are bucketed and raised as AmbiguousIdentifierError (lines 40-47, 72-73). The module's own doc-comment states its purpose is 'failing loudly instead of guessing when an identifier is unknown or ambiguous'. Ids and slugs are also lowercased before matching (lines 34, 37, 51), so `--assistant ID-1` matches a record whose id is `id-1`.
findings.impact: A slug (or id) shared across two projects resolves to whichever catalog entry happened to be paged last, so the wrong assistant or skill is registered with no warning — the exact silent-pick outcome the ambiguity error was added to prevent. With CR-003 leaving project filters inert, cross-project duplicates are reachable on the default path.
findings.recommendation: Bucket slug and id matches the same way names are bucketed and throw AmbiguousIdentifierError when a bucket holds more than one entry; compare ids case-sensitively unless the platform guarantees case-insensitive ids, and align the doc-comment with the matching actually performed.

findings.title: Multi-target --agent never asserted to reach writers
findings.problem: Every headless case in both new test files passes agent: 'claude', which is exactly the default parameter value target: AgentSetupTarget = ['claude'] in registerAssistant and registerSkill, and the register mocks hardcode agentTargets: ['claude']. The only target-related assertion is that resolveAgentSetupTargets was NOT called, so nothing pins that the value parsed from --agent actually reaches the writers.
findings.impact: Dropping the target argument, or passing the wrong one, would still pass the suite. `--agent codex,gemini` could write Claude artifacts only, or persist agentTargets: ['claude'], while the summary line still prints 'Skills are available for Codex, Gemini' — and CR-011's unregister path then deletes artifacts for the wrong target set.
findings.recommendation: Add headless cases with agent: 'codex,gemini' asserting registerSkill/registerAssistant receive ['codex','gemini'] and that the persisted records carry those agentTargets.

findings.title: Headless skills catalog uses different API filters
findings.problem: fetchAllVisibleSkills calls client.skills.listPaginated({ page, per_page: ALL_VISIBLE_PER_PAGE }) with no filters at all, while the wizard's fetchSkills passes filters: { search, project: [], created_by: '', categories: [], visibility: 'public' | null, scope: 'project' | 'marketplace' } (skills/setup/data.ts:88-100) and pages the two scopes separately. Reachability of the consequence is unconfirmed: what the unfiltered server-side default returns is not observable from this repository.
findings.impact: Whatever the unfiltered listing omits becomes indistinguishable from 'not available to you', so a skill the user can install from the wizard can fail headlessly with RegistrationItemNotFoundError; conversely a skill the wizard hides could become resolvable. The same catalog now also backs the interactive fetchSkillsByIds (data.ts:151), so the wizard inherits any divergence.
findings.recommendation: Make the headless crawl page the same scopes and filters the wizard uses (project plus marketplace, merged and de-duplicated by id), or document and test the server's default listing so the two paths are provably the same set.

findings.title: Skills wizard silently drops unavailable ids
findings.problem: fetchSkillsByIds returns allSkills.filter(skill => ids.includes(skill.id)), and setupSkills feeds that filtered list straight into determineChanges(selectedIds, selectedSkills, registeredSkills) (skills/setup/index.ts:143-145). A selected skill that is absent from the fetched catalog is dropped with no error. The assistants path received the equivalent fix in this same change — fetchAssistantsByIds now lets the client.assistants.get rejection propagate (assistants/setup/data.ts:170-176).
findings.impact: Directly unmet acceptance criterion: 'a requested item not available to the authenticated user aborts the entire run with a named, actionable error and a non-zero exit — in both interactive and headless mode'. A run that can reach two of three selected skills prints `Registered 2 skill(s)` and exits 0; if none resolve it prints 'No changes to apply.' The user is told the operation succeeded for items that were never registered.
findings.recommendation: Compare the returned ids against the requested ids in fetchSkillsByIds (or in setupSkills before determineChanges) and throw RegistrationItemNotFoundError for each missing id, matching the assistants path and the one fail-fast contract the spec requires for both modes.

findings.title: Skill availability proven only inside write loop
findings.problem: fetcher.fetchSkillById(skill.id) — the call that actually proves the caller can read the skill — is invoked inside the registerAllOrAbort callback (skills/setup/index.ts:305-309, and in the interactive loop at index.ts:156-164), after earlier items in the batch have already written artifacts. Nothing fetches the skill details for the whole batch before the first write. The assistants path has no equivalent gap because the catalog rows are themselves the registration input.
findings.impact: Unmet acceptance criterion: 'the abort happens before any artifact is written under .claude/.codex/.gemini and before config is saved'. A 403 or 404 on the third of three skills leaves items one and two written under .claude/.codex/.gemini and reports PartialRegistrationError, where the specified contract is a pre-write abort. Combined with CR-011 those two artifacts are also never recorded in config.
findings.recommendation: Fetch every selected skill's detail up front (a pre-flight map of id to SkillDetail) and abort on the first failure before entering registerAllOrAbort, then write from the pre-fetched details.

findings.title: Headless mode can still open a re-auth prompt
findings.problem: Both headless branches call getAuthenticatedClient(config) (assistants/setup/index.ts:196, skills/setup/index.ts:222), which falls back to promptReauthentication on an expired SSO session (src/utils/auth.ts:43-53); the only guard on that prompt is !process.stdin.isTTY (src/providers/core/auth-validation.ts:34). Since headless mode is also entered by flag at a TTY, the guard does not fire. Reachability of the prompt itself was not confirmed by opening those two files in this pass.
findings.impact: Against the acceptance criterion 'a single non-interactive command registers several assistants and/or skills with no prompt and no raw-mode call': `codemie setup assistants -y --assistant a --scope global --agent claude --mode agent` with a stale session blocks on an interactive re-auth prompt instead of failing fast with the actionable re-authentication error, which hangs any scripted or CI caller that still has a TTY attached.
findings.recommendation: Thread the resolved headless decision into the auth path (an explicit nonInteractive option on getAuthenticatedClient) rather than re-deriving it from process.stdin.isTTY, so a flag-triggered headless run fails fast with the 'run codemie profile login' error.
